title: Historical V54 - Gmail Integration
summary: How to connect Gmail, keep a local metadata cache, use multi-account mail workflows, draft or send messages, create reminders, and review confirmation-gated mutations.
html:
Historical reference. See the current V55 architecture guide before using this material.

Gmail Integration

The Gmail integration turns SMTO into a local mail workspace without changing the core runtime boundary. The model can interpret mail intent and draft safe structured actions. The runtime validates those actions, resolves the selected Gmail account, checks scope and confirmation state, and then the Gmail service calls Google APIs with locally stored OAuth tokens.

Use Gmail when email work benefits from the same SMTO operating model as shell work: visible state, local caches, bounded model context, explicit account selection, editable drafts, preview-first mutation, and retained evidence.

flowchart LR U[User] --> UI[Agent UI Mail workspace] UI --> API[Gmail API routes] API --> S[Gmail service] S --> C[Local metadata cache] S --> G[Google Gmail API] UI --> A[gmail.agent capability] A --> V[Runtime validation and confirmation] V --> S

What It Can Do

The current integration supports:

  • direct Gmail OAuth from the Agent UI;
  • optional broker-mode OAuth when a shared broker service is configured;
  • up to 10 connected accounts, each addressable by account_ref;
  • a local SQLite metadata cache for accounts, labels, messages, attachments, senders, drafts, and sync state;
  • manual and background sync with per-account state and sync event history;
  • label, sender, search, selected-message, selected-thread, and current-draft workflows;
  • prompt search over cached metadata plus bounded thread/body context;
  • semantic sender and topic matching with LLM review when simple Gmail queries are not enough;
  • editable compose drafts, reply drafts, transient draft variants, rewrites, and explicit send actions;
  • thread summaries, extraction, selected-thread questions, and Gmail-derived reminder drafts;
  • unsubscribe previews based on Gmail/List-Unsubscribe metadata;
  • confirmation-gated batch mutations such as trash, archive, spam, read/unread, star/unstar, add label, and remove label;
  • account disconnect and local data removal.

Gmail is an advanced integration. It handles personal or business mail, so keep it behind normal runtime review habits: connect only accounts you control, keep OAuth credentials private, and review every mutation before approving it.

Setup

Open the Agent UI and use the Mail or Gmail controls. If Gmail is enabled, the settings/status panel reports configuration, callback URL, connected accounts, sync state, cache counts, labels, and any missing OAuth configuration.

Configuration can come from environment variables, backend settings, or the Gmail OAuth settings panel:

Setting Purpose
AOR_GMAIL_ENABLED Enables or disables the integration. Default is enabled.
AOR_GMAIL_AUTH_MODE direct for local OAuth or broker for broker-assisted auth.
AOR_GMAIL_CLIENT_ID Google OAuth client id for direct auth.
AOR_GMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET Google OAuth client secret for direct auth.
AOR_GMAIL_REDIRECT_URI Explicit callback URL when automatic base-url detection is not enough.
AOR_GMAIL_OAUTH_BROKER_URL Broker base URL when auth mode is broker.
AOR_AGENT_GMAIL_DB_PATH Override for the local Gmail SQLite store.
AOR_GMAIL_AUTH_SECRET_PATH Path for persisted editable OAuth app credentials.
AOR_GMAIL_BACKGROUND_SYNC_ENABLED Enables background cache sync.
AOR_GMAIL_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS Background polling interval, clamped by runtime settings.
AOR_GMAIL_PAGE_SIZE Gmail page size used by sync and list operations.
AOR_GMAIL_SYNC_RECENT_MESSAGE_LIMIT Bounded recent-message sync target.
AOR_GMAIL_WATCH_LABEL_IDS Optional comma-separated label ids to watch.
AOR_GMAIL_PUBSUB_TOPIC_NAME Optional Pub/Sub topic for Gmail watch workflows.
AOR_GMAIL_PUBSUB_SUBSCRIPTION_NAME Optional Pub/Sub subscription for notification pull.
AOR_GMAIL_PUBSUB_CREDENTIALS_PATH Optional Google credentials file for Pub/Sub.

For local development, add OAuth credentials through the UI or environment instead of committing them. If the callback URL is wrong, set AOR_GMAIL_REDIRECT_URI to the exact public or local callback:

https://127.0.0.1:8011/api/agent/gmail/oauth/callback

Use HTTPS when the Agent UI is running with SSL enabled. Google OAuth redirect URIs must match the scheme, host, port, and path.

Accounts And Account References

SMTO can keep multiple Gmail accounts connected. Each account has:

  • account_id, normally derived from the email address;
  • email, display name, nickname, and primary-account flag;
  • granted scopes and token health;
  • per-account sync state and cache rows.

Most Gmail request payloads and query parameters accept account_ref. It may be the account id, email address, or nickname. If no account is specified, the runtime uses the primary connected account when one exists.

The Gmail capability also reads account context from the Mail workspace. If a user says "use my work mailbox" and that wording matches a connected account nickname or address, the runtime resolves that account before it searches or mutates messages.

Sync And Local Cache

Gmail list and prompt-search flows use a local metadata cache first where possible. The cache stores message headers, sender identity, labels, snippets, attachment metadata, draft metadata, and sync bookkeeping. Full message body text is fetched on demand for selected threads or bounded semantic review.

The sync manager can:

  • start a manual full or delta sync;
  • stop a running sync cooperatively;
  • record sync events;
  • recover stale in-flight sync state after backend restart;
  • backfill label-scoped message caches when the UI asks for a view that is not warm yet;
  • run per-account background polling when enabled.

Useful routes:

Route Purpose
GET /api/agent/gmail/accounts Connected account summaries and primary account.
GET /api/agent/gmail/status Configuration, account, sync, labels, and cache status.
POST /api/agent/gmail/sync Start sync, optionally with force_full and account_ref.
POST /api/agent/gmail/sync/stop Request sync cancellation.
GET /api/agent/gmail/sync/events Recent per-account sync events.
GET /api/agent/gmail/labels Gmail labels, optionally refreshed from Google.
GET /api/agent/gmail/messages Cached or Google-backed message lists.
GET /api/agent/gmail/senders Sender inventory from cached metadata.
GET /api/agent/gmail/threads/{thread_id} On-demand selected thread detail.

The cache is local operational state. Do not commit agent_gmail.db if it contains real account metadata.

Mail Workspace

The Agent UI exposes Gmail in two connected forms:

  • the Gmail drawer for setup, account management, prompt search, selected messages, and thread actions;
  • the Mail workspace for a larger mailbox layout with accounts, labels, sender filters, message list, selected thread, composer, queue, and ledger helpers.

Common workflows:

Find security alerts from the last 30 days.

Draft a short reply to the selected thread saying I will review it tomorrow.

Show newsletters that look safe to unsubscribe from.

Create a reminder from this email.

Read-only searches and summaries can answer directly. Drafts remain editable. Sends, trash, archive, label changes, spam marking, read/unread changes, and batch unsubscribe actions require explicit confirmation unless a separate runtime control has already approved the exact visible confirmation prompt.

Drafts, Sends, And Reminders

Draft routes keep editing and sending separate:

Route Purpose
POST /api/agent/gmail/drafts Create a new editable compose draft.
PATCH /api/agent/gmail/drafts/{draft_id} Update a compose draft.
POST /api/agent/gmail/drafts/reply Create an editable reply draft.
PATCH /api/agent/gmail/drafts/{draft_id}/reply Update a reply draft.
POST /api/agent/gmail/replies/suggest Ask the configured LLM for editable reply text.
POST /api/agent/gmail/messages/suggest Ask the configured LLM for editable new-message text.
POST /api/agent/gmail/compose/variants Generate transient compose or reply variants.
POST /api/agent/gmail/drafts/{draft_id}/send Send a saved Gmail draft.
POST /api/agent/gmail/replies/send Send a reply from visible editable text.
POST /api/agent/gmail/messages/send Send a new message from visible editable text.
POST /api/agent/gmail/reminders/draft Extract an editable reminder proposal from a thread.
POST /api/agent/gmail/reminders Save a Gmail-derived reminder as an SMTO event.

The model should not invent recipients, commitments, dates, attachments, or facts. It receives bounded visible thread context and explicit user instructions, then returns editable content.

Safety Boundaries

Gmail follows the same trust pattern as the rest of SMTO:

Actor Owns
LLM Intent interpretation, semantic matching, draft text, summaries, and variant suggestions.
Runtime Account resolution, typed payload validation, confirmation state, trace evidence, and policy.
Gmail service OAuth tokens, local cache, Google API calls, sync, and message mutation.
User Account connection, final approval, edited draft text, and send/mutation decisions.

Mutation operations are preview-first. The runtime can show matched messages, unsubscribe methods, candidate counts, batch progress, rollback guidance, and confirmation details before any mutation is applied.

Typical confirmation-gated operations:

  • send_draft;
  • trash;
  • archive;
  • mark_spam;
  • mark_read;
  • mark_unread;
  • star and unstar;
  • add_label and remove_label;
  • unsubscribe;
  • broad or batch cleanups.

The Gmail capability may use semantic matching for requests such as "marketing emails" or "messages that likely need a reply." Semantic matching is evidence, not authority. Current cache contents, selected account, Gmail query results, runtime policy, and user approval still decide what happens.

Troubleshooting

If Gmail does not connect:

  • open the Gmail status panel and check missing configuration;
  • verify the callback URL exactly matches the OAuth app redirect URI;
  • verify AOR_GMAIL_AUTH_MODE is direct or broker;
  • verify the browser is using HTTPS when SSL is enabled;
  • reconnect the account if token health is expired or missing.

If mail does not appear:

  • run POST /api/agent/gmail/sync from the UI sync button;
  • check /api/agent/gmail/sync/events;
  • confirm the selected account_ref;
  • refresh labels;
  • search with a smaller label or sender scope.

If an action is blocked:

  • read the confirmation card and matched message list;
  • confirm the account and selected thread/message ids;
  • review the trace details for validation or Gmail API errors;
  • approve only if the preview is the operation you intended.
